correctness.rationale: After XOR translation to s0=0, every zero-fixing cube automorphism permutes coordinates, and fixing other marked vertices allows permutations only within identical binary mark-signature blocks. Orbit invariant a_t(x) is each block Hamming weight; sizes are products of binomial coefficients. Ordinary 1-WL at round d records distances to each marked vertex by neighbour-layer induction. At round d+1 its neighbour distance differences are ±(1,1−2t_1,...), and these signed vectors are injective in t and the bit direction, recovering every a_t exactly; equivariance prohibits further splitting inside an orbit. Distinct signatures iff trivial orbit partition. Pigeonhole gives r−1≥ceil(log2 d), and binary coordinate codes realize equality with distinct marks. Independent standard 1-WL vs orbit-profile partitions checked on 760 marked-set examples d≤5. This is finite corroboration, not proof of all d.
